steps.effect_text: On zinc plating Zn-N bonds form at pyridinic-nitrogen sites, moving their chemical state toward graphitic nitrogen
all_effect_text: On zinc plating Zn-N bonds form at pyridinic-nitrogen sites, moving their chemical state toward graphitic nitrogen
Pyridinic nitrogen, rather than graphitic nitrogen or bare graphitic carbon, is the electrochemically active zincophilic site
Zinc adsorbs as single atoms that seed clusters, which expand into a mesoporous zinc network
Plated zinc coexists on the carbon host as dispersed single atoms, ~1 nm clusters and extended porous networks
Plated zinc is planar and compact on CnC HS but forms a dense mat of sharp dendritic platelets on C HS

observations: After zinc deposition the ~398 eV N 1s feature collapses and the ~401 eV feature becomes the taller of the two
The sharp 290.1 eV C 1s feature of pristine CnC HS is absent after zinc deposition, while the 284.9 and 288.3 eV features remain
The ~1200 cm-1 Raman feature weakens from the pristine trace at the top of the stack to the zinc-loaded trace at the bottom
Zinc on CnC HS is a largely flat deposit with sparse protruding platelets; on C HS the surface is a dense mat of sharp platelets
HAADF-STEM of zinc-loaded carbon shows bright zinc at three scales: isolated points, ~1 nm blobs and extended lattice-resolved patches
